scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: Formerly Important
cards.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've rung my old headteacher's bell. Why is nobody lining up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This is your retirement lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lunch still benefits from orderly pupils.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're your former colleagues.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should require less supervision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought my headteacher's bell to the retirement lunch. Shall I ring everyone into their seats?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sit down. I promised the caterers we'd start at one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the register. I'll find who's holding us up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a buffet. Your former colleagues can serve themselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll appoint table monitors. They can report to me before anyone takes seconds.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 rings the old headteacher's bell, and A3/A5 retain supervisory expectations despite B2's retirement reminder.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 turns B2's lunch into an occasion for order; A5 uses B4's former-colleague status to demand less supervision.

relationship.evidence: B4 asserts that the guests are colleagues, challenging A's treatment of them as pupils.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4's claim to adult equality into a stricter expectation of obedience.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a bell and attempted lineup; B2 promptly locates them at A's retirement lunch.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'less supervision' economically preserves the former headteacher's sincere logic.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 brings a headteacher's bell to retirement; A3 requests a register and A5 appoints monitors despite lacking present authority.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's start time prompts A3's attendance check, although nobody is established as late; B4's buffet prompts A5's supervision of seconds.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to honor the caterers' schedule; B4 defends former colleagues' freedom to serve themselves, changing A's supervisory tactic.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes the need for organized seating; A5 expands A's authority into delegated monitoring and permission for seconds.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a retirement lunch and a retained school bell; B2 adds a concrete catering deadline and B4 establishes buffet service.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's register and A5's table monitors economically translate school authority into lunch management; A5's extra control earns the joke.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies a scheduled start; A3 applies the former headteacher's attendance procedure to identify supposed holdouts.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 reveals self-service and rejects management of colleagues; A5 adapts by appointing monitors over buffet seconds.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 retain the equipment, procedures and expectation of obedience belonging to A's former role.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves from personally ringing a bell to installing subordinate monitors who report to A.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A carries the disciplinary expectations of a former headteacher into a retirement gathering that no longer grants that authority.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General bossiness: B2's retirement lunch and B4's former colleagues specifically establish authority that has expired.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 retains an old occupational bell, and A5 continues supervising after B2 and B4 explicitly remove the role's present support.

records.recommendedEdit: Preserved the original firstPass exactly. The supplied candidate review identifies limited heightening and a corrective B; this retry replaces the whole exchange within the retirement-lunch setting, adding a catering deadline and buffet. Separate internal reread, coach-1.0: fidelity 5 (A1 brings the former office's bell; A3 requests a register; A5 installs monitors), logic 5 (B2's deadline causes A3's attendance check; B4's self-service arrangement causes A5's delegated monitoring), relationship 4 (B2 must meet a catering commitment and B4 offers a workable meal arrangement), heightening 4 (A5 expands from calling people to seats into a reporting system governing seconds), specificity 5 (A1 establishes the retirement lunch; B2 supplies its deadline), brevity 4 (A5's seconds restriction follows school supervision). Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, 74 words; hard gates pass. Alternative b turns a successor's invitation into commercial approval; this version turns a host's practical accommodation into school discipline. No live, independent or runtime testing performed.
records.remainingConcern: A3 assumes someone is delaying lunch when B2 chiefly asks A to sit down. This is a small character-driven inference. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: The register request assumes A expects school records at a social meal; it needs habitual confidence. The unchanged distinguishingEvidence field describes the original turn placement; the revised retirement context is explicit in A1.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved shop alternative uses checking and approval to retain authority over a successor. This candidate uses school discipline over former colleagues in a social setting.

cards.title: Formerly Important
cards.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings to me, as usual.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold the shop last year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I kept the counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That doesn't make you the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the money still fit?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings over. I've put out my counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold me the shop last year. I count them now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Bring your total and I'll check it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I came to invite you to our anniversary sale.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Already a year? Leave me the proposed discounts. I'll approve them before you print.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 expects the takings as usual and A3 retains the counting tray, but A5 turns that habit into a strained ownership argument.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's sale with a retained object; A5 addresses B4's ownership objection through that object's physical fit.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 defend the consequences of the shop sale against A's continuing demands.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats the tray's supposed authority without adding a concrete new expectation or consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes shop takings and A3 gives A a playable counting tray.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'money still fit' is brief but feels more like an object joke than a former owner's habitual conduct.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 prepares the counting tray; after B2 establishes the sale, A3 claims checking authority and A5 claims discount approval.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 turns B2's independent counting into subordinate reporting; A5 turns B4's anniversary sale invitation into a pricing review.

relationship.evidence: B2 asserts current ownership while B4 offers a social invitation; A repeatedly converts goodwill into managerial access.

heightening.evidence: B4 opens a fresh topic, and A5 expands from checking cash totals to authorizing future commercial decisions.

specificity.evidence: A1's counting tray, B2's sale last year and B4's anniversary event establish concrete history and business activity.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Good' quietly refuses the transfer of power, and A5's approval deadline earns its humor through that same assumption.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 says the buyer now counts takings; A3 positions the former owner as reviewer of those totals.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 introduces the anniversary sale; A5 demands its proposed discounts for approval.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A carries former ownership expectations into an encounter with the actual owner.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A uses a friendly invitation to reclaim authority over an additional business function.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats the sale of a former business as though it transferred tasks while leaving A's supervisory authority intact.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: A current owner delegating work: B2 explicitly says the shop was sold to B last year, yet A3 and A5 still demand oversight.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 recasts the new owner's counting as subordinate work; A5 treats B4's social invitation as a request for pricing approval.

records.recommendedEdit: The revision replaces the detachable physical-fit joke with continued occupational behavior and adds an anniversary invitation within the existing shop setting. Second internal read: fidelity 5 (A3/A5), logic 5 (B2/A3; B4/A5), relationship 5 (B owns the shop and offers an invitation), heightening 4 (A5 claims pricing approval), specificity 5 (A1/B2), brevity 4 (A5); total 95. Hard gates pass; under 75 words.
records.remainingConcern: The precise personal relationship beyond seller and buyer is open, but playable. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A's persistence should sound habitual and helpful, not like a deliberate attempt to reverse the sale.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b moves between accounting and pricing through a successor's goodwill; a preserves school discipline through corrections.

cards.title: One Mistake from Gone
cards.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's my first lunch order as supervisor. Is soup too indecisive?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what a confident supervisor would say.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Order what you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you witness that instruction before I risk the soup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch as supervisor. If I order soup, will they think promoting me was a mistake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promoted you. I'm having soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then soup. Unless copying you proves I can't lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Choose mine too. I need to take this call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both lunches? Right. Does choosing the bread count toward whether I keep the job?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 worries whether soup appears indecisive, but A5 seeks a witnessed instruction without clearly making continued belonging the issue.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 interprets B2's reassurance as supervisory confidence; A5 turns B4's permission into something requiring a witness.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 reassure A but reveal little beyond wanting A to make an ordinary lunch choice.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates from worrying about soup to requiring formal protection before ordering it.

specificity.evidence: A1 immediately establishes a newly promoted supervisor choosing lunch.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'risk the soup' efficiently exposes disproportionate anxiety tied to the established order.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes soup evidence against promotion; A3 fears copying disproves leadership; A5 makes bread a retention test.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's own soup choice prompts A3's imitation dilemma; B4 delegates both lunches, prompting A5's anxiety about expanded responsibility.

relationship.evidence: B2 has actual promotion authority and reassures A; B4 needs a call handled and entrusts A with ordering.

heightening.evidence: B4 increases A's responsibility from one lunch to both, and A5 reads that trust as a test of continued employment.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a first lunch as supervisor; B4's call supplies a plausible immediate reason for delegation.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's copying dilemma follows the card neatly; A5's explicit job question slightly repeats A1's stated anxiety.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 establishes the promoter's soup choice, which A3 first adopts and then treats as evidence of inadequate leadership.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 delegates ordering while taking a call; A5 makes the enlarged assignment and bread choice a job-retention examination.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A repeatedly translates ordinary decisions into judgments about deserving the supervisory role.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: Reassurance becomes delegated trust, which A experiences as a more consequential test.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats an ordinary lunch decision as evidence that could invalidate A's newly earned position.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Generic indecision: revised A1 fears the promotion was a mistake and A5 explicitly connects bread selection to keeping the job.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B2's reassurance becomes A3's fear of failing leadership through imitation; B4's delegated choice becomes A5's employment test.

records.recommendedEdit: The original needs a clearer connection between decisions and deserving the role. The revision retains lunch and adds B as the promoting manager. Second internal read: fidelity 5 (A1/A5), logic 5 (B2/A3; B4/A5), relationship 4 (B4 needs to take a call), heightening 4 (A5 now chooses for both), specificity 5 (A1/B2), brevity 4 (A3); total 92. Hard gates pass; under 75 words.
records.remainingConcern: A5 repeats the employment stakes explicitly instead of discovering a subtler manifestation. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5 states the fear directly; performance should keep it a sincere question rather than an explanation of the card.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a places anxiety before the actual promoter; b projects managerial judgment onto an uninvolved driver.

cards.title: Protection Has Terms
cards.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow my car if I approve every stop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm visiting my sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A safe first destination. Send me the return plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I decide that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while enjoying my comprehensive support package.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrow my car. I'll feel better if we agree every stop first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just my sister's, then home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Text before leaving hers so I can approve the traffic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She might need me to stay overnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Give me her number; I'll arrange your bedtime so you're safe to drive.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes borrowing conditional on approval of every stop, and A3 explicitly evaluates the sister's address as safe.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's sister visit to demand a return plan; A5 rejects B4's autonomy but adds little specific response.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants transport to a sister and B4 wants control of the return journey.

heightening.evidence: A5 renames the control already established in A1/A3 a 'comprehensive support package' without changing its reach.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a car loan and B2 supplies a straightforward family visit.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's corporate support-package phrase is concise but substitutes a label for a developed protective demand.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 conditions the car loan on approved stops; A3 controls departure; A5 extends protective supervision to bedtime.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's sister visit supplies A3's departure checkpoint; B4's overnight possibility supplies A5's sleep-control plan.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers an itinerary and B4 introduces a family need; A accommodates both while imposing new conditions.

heightening.evidence: B4's overnight stay moves A5's control beyond the car and into the sister's household and B's bedtime.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a car loan and B2 the route; A5's request for the sister's number creates a playable next demand.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's kindly 'Of course' precedes an intrusive bedtime arrangement; A3's 'approve the traffic' is somewhat mannered.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies the sister's home as the stop; A3 requires permission before leaving it.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 raises staying overnight; A5 seeks the sister's number to control rest before driving.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A offers support sincerely while making its safety depend on A's continuing authority.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A's route supervision expands into control of an overnight household arrangement.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A offers caring support on terms that require continuing control over the recipient's choices.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary caution about lending a car: A3 requires approval to depart and A5 extends control into B's bedtime at another person's home.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised B4's possible overnight stay produces A5's new control over sleep, explicitly justified as safe driving.

records.recommendedEdit: The original final beat labels the game instead of developing it. The revision retains the car and sister visit, adding a possible overnight stay. Second internal read: fidelity 5 (A1/A3/A5), logic 5 (B2/A3; B4/A5), relationship 4 (B4 needs flexibility), heightening 5 (A5 reaches into bedtime), specificity 5 (A1/B2), brevity 4 (A5); total 95. Hard gates pass; under 75 words.
records.remainingConcern: 'Approve the traffic' needs performance to mean approving departure conditions. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: Approving traffic is deliberately disproportionate and needs a sincerely caring tone.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a controls private travel and sleep; b uses financial patronage to supervise an artist's professional exposure.

cards.title: Protection Has Terms
cards.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll back your exhibition, provided I choose the guest list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's controlling the exhibition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Protecting it from unsuitable viewers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's about independence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me make independence safe for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fund your exhibition. Let me choose the guests so nobody undermines you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need critics there. That's how I get another show.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send me their names. I'll find the encouraging ones.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The main critic won't promise a good review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sit beside her. You can concentrate on being independent while I handle her questions.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 conditions backing on selecting guests and A3 reframes control as protection from unsuitable viewers.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's control objection with protection; A5 takes B4's independence theme into the same justification.

relationship.evidence: B2 defends ownership of the exhibition and B4 gives independence as an artistic stake.

heightening.evidence: A5 says 'make independence safe' without specifying a new term or practical consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes exhibition funding and guest selection, but A5 remains abstract.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's paradox summarizes A's position neatly but does not earn a new playable move.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 funds the exhibition under guest control; A3 screens critics; A5 offers protection by taking over their questions.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's need for critics changes A3's tactic to screening them; B4's uncooperative main critic changes A5's tactic to direct supervision.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs credible criticism to secure another show, while A1's funding gives A leverage over that professional need.

heightening.evidence: B4 defeats promised encouragement, so A5 advances from controlling attendance to managing the live conversation.

specificity.evidence: A1's funded exhibition and B2's next-show stakes are clear; A5 offers a concrete seating and question-handling tactic.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's promise to let B 'concentrate on being independent' grows from the patron's sincere control, though the irony is overt.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 establishes critics as necessary; A3 accommodates their presence through selective approval.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 makes a favorable review unavailable as a condition; A5 substitutes personal supervision of the critic.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Every form of offered support preserves the funder's control over B's exposure.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: Screening protective conditions develops into occupying the artist's own professional conversation.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A makes artistic support conditional on managing the people and scrutiny that might threaten B.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Simple censorship: A1 offers funding as protection, and A5 presents taking over questions as a service enabling B's independence.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B4 blocks preapproval of a critic's opinion, so A5 replaces guest selection with direct supervision of the critic.

records.recommendedEdit: The revision gives B a concrete career need and makes the final protective condition actionable. Critics are new illustrative details within the existing exhibition setting. Second internal read: fidelity 5 (A1/A5), logic 5 (B2/A3; B4/A5), relationship 5 (B2 needs another show), heightening 4 (A5 personally intervenes), specificity 5 (A1/B2), brevity 4 (A5); total 95. Hard gates pass; under 75 words.
records.remainingConcern: The final independence wording is conspicuously ironic but remains sincere character logic. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5's use of 'independent' carries irony that A must not knowingly acknowledge.
records.alternativeComparison: Compared with a's personal loan, b gives B a career need that directly conflicts with the protection being offered.

cards.title: Chosen by Power
cards.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. Should I join her table now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She says hello to everybody.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then she'll recognise me when you introduce us properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She doesn't know your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. There's still room for a memorable introduction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. That means I can sit at her table, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating donors. She says hello to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me again. If she remembers me, you'll know I belong there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked you to bring over that empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She picked me. I'll carry it over and ask which side of her I should sit.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats a mayoral greeting as grounds to join her table, but A5 emphasizes getting noticed more than proving belonging.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 converts B2's ordinary greeting into recognition; A5 uses B4's unknown name as room for an introduction.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 puncture A's assumptions but give B no stated responsibility or stake.

heightening.evidence: A5 requests a memorable introduction after A3 already requests a proper introduction.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a mayor and her table, while the larger event remains unspecified.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's optimistic use of not being known follows A's established eagerness without excess wording.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats the mayor's greeting as belonging; A3 seeks recognition; A5 treats a chair-carrying request as personal selection.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 devalues the generic greeting, prompting A3's memory test; B4's chair request prompts A5's bid to sit beside the mayor.

relationship.evidence: B2 controls donor seating and resists A's claim; B4 supplies a legitimate task that A tries to convert into access.

heightening.evidence: After B4, A5 uses a service task as evidence of special belonging and a route to a specific seat.

specificity.evidence: A1's mayoral table, B2's donor seating and B4's empty chair give actors a clear event and physical objective.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'She picked me' economically misreads the errand before turning it into a seating negotiation.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 says everyone gets a greeting; A3 seeks a second introduction to prove individual recognition.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 supplies the mayor's chair-carrying request; A5 interprets being asked as selection and seeks adjacent seating.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A pursues influential attention and repeatedly turns it into proof of belonging.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: The desire for recognition becomes an attempt to convert service into a place at the mayor's side.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A pursues the mayor's attention and converts ordinary acknowledgment into proof of admission to her circle.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General networking: A3 explicitly makes being remembered proof of belonging, and A5 treats a chair-moving request as personal selection.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised B4 offers a mundane task from the mayor; A5 interprets that attention as permission to sit beside her.

records.recommendedEdit: The original repeats its introduction tactic. The revision gives B a seating responsibility and adds a chair request at the existing mayoral event. Second internal read: fidelity 5 (A3/A5), logic 5 (B2/A3; B4/A5), relationship 4 (B2 seats donors), heightening 4 (A5 turns service into seating entitlement), specificity 5 (A1/B2), brevity 4 (A5); total 92. Hard gates pass; under 75 words.
records.remainingConcern: A5's seating inference is deliberately large, but the empty chair makes it playable. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: Both alternatives exploit a minor service for an influential person, although their desired outcomes and B's roles differ.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a negotiates actual access with a seating organizer; b seeks photographic evidence of association.

cards.title: Chosen by Power
cards.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A position of trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's taking it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then photograph the handover. It shows we work closely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm photographing her team. She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her my name. She should know who she's trusting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now she wants you to bring her bag to the car. You're blocking my shot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take both. Ask if she wants me beside her in the car. She clearly needs me on the team.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 seeks proximity to the director, A3 calls coat-holding trust, and A5 presents a handover as proof of working closely.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 directly reinterprets B2's coat task; A5 makes B4's withdrawal of that task a new photographic opportunity.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges A's claim to placement and B4 reports the director reclaiming the coat, removing A's foothold.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns the loss of apparent access in B4 into a request to manufacture stronger evidence of access.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a group photo and B2 supplies the director's coat as a concrete status token.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's three-word claim and A5's handover request derive their wit directly from the coat's changing significance.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 seeks proximity to the director; A3 requests personal recognition for holding her coat; A5 treats another errand as proof that A belongs on her team.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's coat assignment becomes A3's claim of personal trust. B4's bag-to-car request causes A5 to carry both items and seek a seat beside the director in that car.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects the team photograph's membership boundary, and B4's 'You're blocking my shot' gives the photographer an immediate practical reason to move A.

heightening.evidence: B4 redirects A away from the photograph toward an errand; A5 uses that exclusion to pursue closer access in the director's car and explicitly claim team membership.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a group photo naturally; B2 identifies the photographer's remit and coat assignment, while B4 provides the bag and car that make A5 immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'who she's trusting' efficiently recasts coat holding as recognition; A5's 'She clearly needs me on the team' earns its irony from B4's additional menial request.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies A as the director's coat holder rather than team member; A3 seeks an introduction by framing that assignment as personal trust.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 adds the bag errand and specifies the car. A5 accepts both carrying duties and turns the destination into a new bid for privileged proximity.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A seeks the director's notice through the photographer and reads delegated errands as evidence of belonging, explicitly stated in A5.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: Denied photographic proximity, A uses B4's new assignment to pursue shared travel beside the director, extending the same attention-as-membership behavior.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A inflates a powerful person's minor attention into visible evidence of belonging to that person's working circle.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Public Respect: A3 and A5 seek evidence of the director's personal trust and closeness, rather than public acknowledgment of A's own established standing.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B2's coat request becomes A3's 'position of trust'; B4's reclamation becomes A5's evidence that they 'work closely.'

records.recommendedEdit: Preserved the exact original firstPass. Before drafting, the distinguishing mechanism is pursuing influential attention as proof of membership: unlike Public Respect, A3 wants the director to learn A's name and A5 seeks continued personal access through her errands.
